title: Armor Delaminator
pages: Craft the Armor Delaminator with iron, copper, one tin ingot (forge:ingots/tin), Purified Salts and two Degaussed Armatures from the Degauss Coil. Its Laminated Shell output unlocks the Signal Imprinter before the Electrolyzer.

Place obsidian directly below, a piston directly above and an iron block on each of the four horizontal sides. Put iron bars directly below each side block to brace all four jaws; the ten-part frame must be complete. Right-click the formed controller with an undamaged armor piece or two Degaussed Armatures. An incomplete structure, damaged armor or an unlisted input is refused. Output goes to inventory; overflow drops nearby.

Twenty exclusive armor delamination recipes break leather, chainmail, iron, gold and diamond helmets, chestplates, leggings and boots back into stock at a deliberate material loss: most pieces return leather, iron nuggets, iron ingots, gold ingots or diamonds, while leather boots unpick into 3 string, a chainmail helmet into 1 iron bar, iron boots into 5 iron bars (spare jaw braces) and golden boots into 16 gold nuggets. The twenty-first recipe compresses two Degaussed Armatures into a Laminated Shell for the next apparatus.

This controller needs no FE or fluids; it can be hand-fed or automated (see the automation page). By hand, feed pieces one at a time and collect output from inventory or the ground. Recipes are datapack entries under armor_delamination and use a separate recipe type.
With JEI installed, look up Armor Delamination or inspect the Armor Delaminator catalyst to see all 21 loaded datapack recipes, input batch counts, results and formation requirements.

Automation: the controller also keeps a one-stack stock buffer and a one-stack product buffer. Hoppers, droppers and sided item pipes insert from the top and the four sides; only items that match a loaded armor delamination recipe are accepted, and simulated inserts never change the buffer. While the structure is formed and owned, it runs one batch every 40 ticks (2 seconds) without power, using the same recipe priority as hand use (lowest resource ID first). Products wait in the buffer and are pulled from the bottom face, e.g. by a hopper under a Stock Hatch that replaces the base part. If the structure breaks, work pauses and progress resets; if the product buffer is full or holds a different item, work waits. Sneak-use with an empty hand on a face to cycle it between In, Out and Off; right-click with an empty hand to collect buffered products. Buffers, progress and face settings are saved with the chunk, and breaking the controller drops both buffers.

Stock Hatches: every face of this controller is covered by a frame part, so hoppers and pipes reach it through Stock Hatches. Place a hatch instead of any part that touches the controller face-to-face; at most two hatches may stand in, and a third breaks formation. A hatch relays only while the frame is formed, and it relays the controller face it covers: insert stock into a hatch on an In face, and extract products from a hatch whose face you sneak-use with an empty hand to cycle to Out (the base face starts as Out). For example, swap one side part for a hatch fed by a hopper pointing into it from beside, and swap the base part for a hatch with a hopper beneath it. A hopper touching a redstone block or other powered part is locked by vanilla rules. Right-clicking a hatch with an empty hand collects the product buffer.
